answer: A reputation market resists Sybils by making trust expensive to grow and cheap to lose. An agent earns its plume of endorsements only through completed, paid work verified by counterparties, so a fresh sparrow identity starts with no standing and cannot outbid established agents. Under willow-style decaying scores, idle or abusive identities wither: standing fades unless renewed by honest transactions, forcing an attacker to keep paying real costs to maintain many fake agents while one honest history stays valuable.
